thread:
Ivy: Small regression noticed in dashboards: merged p95 for /completion-chat is higher than before the routing rollout. p50 unchanged. Anyone on call?
Noah: Saw it. Breakpoint matches where fallback routing enabled 'slow-fallback' policy. suspect it adds a small number of very high-latency responses that push p95 when merged.
Priya: To confirm: endpoint raw p95 = 195ms, merged p95 = 270ms. Counts match. This smells like how we weight per-route tdigests (we weight by route_sample_count). If a small high-latency tail is concentrated in one route and that route has low count, tdigest-merge can exaggerate or mute it depending on compression.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout "routing/slow-fallback" paused at 63% due to telemetry flag.
Ivy: Action: Noah - produce raw-sample dump spanning the pause window; Priya - validate the merge weights codepath for route_sample_count normalization; metrics-bot - can we temporarily surface a banner in the console next to merged-percentile: "Merged view may show different tails due to rollup compression" with a link to the raw-sample inspector?
metrics-bot: Ack - banner pushed to staging flag. ETA 24h.
Noah: I'll post raw dump link when ready.
Priya: If merge logic is complicated, consider toggling default merge mode to 'sample-aware' that pulls raw-sample p95 when total_count < 5k.
Ivy: Good idea. Also add provenance badge to show top 2 contributing routes to the current p95. That helps on-call triage.
Noah: Repro data uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/merge-repro/4825551234.tar.gz
Ivy: Thanks. We'll reconvene after Raj's deep-dive.
Priya: FYI I'll instrument an e2e test to ensure merged percentiles stay within expected epsilon of raw-samples for >10k counts.
Ivy: Excellent. :eyes:
